title: Turn any commit into a version string
summary: git describe answers 'which release is this build from, and how far past it'. It is how build systems stamp version numbers without a version file to maintain.
mental_model: `describe` walks backwards from a commit until it finds a tag, then reports `<tag>-<commits since>-g<sha>`. Exactly at a tag you get just the tag — which is what makes it a usable version string.

steps.title: Describe where you are
steps.why: Two commits past v1.1.0. The output reads `v1.1.0-2-g<sha>`: nearest tag, distance, and the abbreviated commit — everything a build stamp needs, generated rather than maintained.
steps.expect: v1.1.0-2-g followed by a short sha.

verify.label: describe reports the nearest tag and the distance

steps.title: Describe exactly at a tag
steps.why: On the tagged commit itself there is no distance and no sha — you get the bare tag. This is what makes `git describe` safe to use directly as a version: release builds get clean numbers.

verify.label: a tagged commit describes as the bare tag

steps.title: Include a dirty marker
steps.why: `--dirty` appends a suffix when the working tree has uncommitted changes. A build stamped `v1.1.0-2-gabc1234-dirty` tells you immediately it was not built from committed code.
steps.expect: -dirty appears, then disappears once the change is discarded.

steps.title: Handle repositories with no tags
steps.why: Plain `describe` fails outright when it finds no tag, which breaks builds. `--always` falls back to the bare sha, and `--tags` lets it use lightweight tags too.
steps.expect: Without --tags the lightweight nightly tag is ignored; with it, it wins.

verify.label: --tags makes lightweight tags visible to describe
verify.hint: git tag nightly-... creates a lightweight tag; describe ignores it by default

steps.title: Ask the opposite question
steps.why: `--contains` reports the first tag that comes *after* a commit — 'which release did this fix ship in'. It is the query you run when a customer asks whether a fix is out yet.
steps.expect: The pump commit is contained in v1.1.0.

verify.label: you can find which release contains a commit

steps.title: Restrict which tags count
steps.why: `--match` filters by pattern, so release tags win over nightlies. This is how a build script produces `v1.1.0-2-g...` regardless of what other tags exist.

verify.label: pattern matching ignores the nightly tag

steps.title: Stamp a build
steps.why: One command produces the version, written into a file the application can read. No manual version bumping, no file to forget to update — the tag is the single source of truth.

verify.label: the build stamp was generated from the tag
describe produces a version string from the nearest release tag
verify.hint: git describe --match 'v[0-9]*' to ignore nightly tags

verify.label: a tagged commit gives the bare tag
--contains answers which release a commit shipped in
a build stamp file was generated

pitfalls: `git describe` fails with an error in a repo with no tags. Always pass `--always` in build scripts.
It ignores lightweight tags unless you pass `--tags`. Half the 'describe does not see my tag' reports are this.
A shallow clone (CI default on some platforms) may not contain the tag at all. Fetch with `--tags --unshallow` first.
`--dirty` only notices tracked-file changes. An untracked file does not make the tree dirty by this measure.
cheatsheet: mark builds from an unclean tree
fall back to a sha when there is no tag
